title: Assisted Hatching
content: Assisted hatching is an IVF technique in which the zona is treated prior to embryo transfer in order to weaken the wall of the embryo and thus improve the likelihood of successful hatching and embryo implantation.
Assisted hatching has demonstrated the potential for improving embryo implantation rates and clinical pregnancy rates in selected patient groups undergoing IVF.

title: Fertility Enhancing Surgeries Myomectomy
content: It is the least minimally invasive surgery to extract uterine fibroids. A hysteroscope, which is a rigid scope with an operative element, is inserted into the uterus through the cervix and vagina. The hydroscope removes the fibroid without incisions and offers the fastest recovery among the three methods.
The patient is either under general anaesthesia or mild sedation. Hospitalisation is not required since the procedure is completed within 90 minutes, and the recovery takes 48 hours.

The disadvantage of hysteroscopic myomectomy is that it can only be performed on select candidates who fulfil certain conditions. To be eligible for the procedure, the fibroids should be smaller than 4 centimetres, submucosal and not be deep in the uterine wall.

title: Hysteroscopic Surgery Tubal Cannulation
content: Unlike fallopian tube surgery, an invasive surgery requiring cuts, tubal cannulation uses a catheter inserted into the body through the vagina and the cervix, requiring no incisions or hospitalisation.

A hysteroscopy or laparoscopy guides the catheter into the uterine cavity to find the fallopian tube opening. The doctor uses a hysterosalpingogram to flush dye through the catheter and identify the area of blockage.

Following this, tubal cannulation is conducted where an inflatable balloon is attached to the tip of the catheter, which passes the proximal portion of the Fallopian tube and is used to open the blockage.

title: Vitrification
content: Vitrification was first investigated and described in the 19th century. Luyet, the founder of cryobiology, first recognized the potential of achieving an ice-free, structurally arrested state for cryopreservation2,3. Subsequently, it was recognized that vitrification would be a better technique for the preservation of living cells and tissues than would solutions that crystallize and hence damage cells during cooling and warming.

Vitrification can be defined as a physical process by which a highly concentrated solution of cryoprotectant solidifies into a glassy vitrified state from the liquid phase by an extreme elevation in the viscosity while cooling at a low temperature. The solid which is called glass retains the normal molecular and ionic distribution of the liquid state and can be considered to be an extremely viscous supercooled liquid4.

content: Polycystic Ovarian Disease (PCOD) or Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a common hormonal disorder affecting women of reproductive age. It can lead to irregular menstrual cycles, weight gain, excess hair growth, and fertility issues.
Our comprehensive approach involves lifestyle management, dietary guidance, and medical treatments to regulate hormones, restore ovulation, and improve overall health and fertility.

title: Fibroid Issues
content: Uterine fibroids are non-cancerous growths of the uterus that often appear during childbearing years. While many women with fibroids have no symptoms, others may experience heavy bleeding, pelvic pain, or reproductive issues.

We provide expert care for uterine fibroids, offering treatments ranging from medication to minimally invasive surgeries like hysteroscopic or laparoscopic myomectomy to preserve fertility and alleviate symptoms.

title: Tubal Blocks
content: Blocked fallopian tubes are a common cause of female infertility, preventing the sperm and egg from meeting or the fertilized egg from reaching the uterus.

Diagnosis typically involves a hysterosalpingogram (HSG) or laparoscopy. Depending on the location and extent of the blockage, treatments such as laparoscopic surgery, tubal cannulation, or IVF may be recommended.

title: Embryo Freezing
content: Embryo freezing, or cryopreservation, allows individuals and couples to store viable embryos from an IVF cycle for future use. This provides the opportunity to attempt another pregnancy without undergoing the full ovarian stimulation process again.
Using advanced vitrification techniques, embryos are rapidly frozen and stored in liquid nitrogen, ensuring high survival rates upon thawing.

title: Endometriosis
content: Endometriosis is a condition where tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus, causing pain and often contributing to infertility.
Our specialized treatments focus on managing pain and improving fertility through medications or advanced laparoscopic surgeries to remove endometrial tissue and adhesions.

content: Recurrent pregnancy loss can be emotionally devastating. It requires a thorough evaluation to identify underlying causes, which may include genetic, structural, hormonal, or immunological factors.
